parts:
Hi,

I have a problem where I want to sample from a distribution that is loosely speaking a "two-sided Gaussian" -- it is composed of the left half of a gaussian of width sigma2 and the right half of a gaussian of width sigma 1. The right half is to be scaled so that its peak is the same as that of the left. So the distribution looks like a Gaussian that is asymmetric about its peak.

I think a way to do this is to use a mixture of two truncated Gaussians with mixture fractions equal to sigma1/(sigma1+sigma2) and sigma2/(sigma1+sigma2)

The distribution for the left side is y ~ normal(mu,sigma1) T[,mu], so that it has support only on the left side of the peak
The distribution for the right side is y ~ normal(mu,sigma2) T[mu,], so that it has support only on the right side of the peak

I implemented the mixture by drawing a uniform random variable called mixingParam; if it's less than sigma1/(sigma1+sigma2), I draw from the first distribution and otherwise I draw from the second.

The complication is that y and mu and sigma are really vectors.

After reading the sections in the Stan manual about truncated distributions and mixtures, I implemented this in my Stan model.
The PyStan code is included below:  I've included the entire Stan model, but the relevant part is in the parameters and model blocks.

The model compiles, but it doesn't sample, returning the error below.

Any help to correctly implement this sampling would be appreciated!

Cheers,

Joe Catanzarite

Hi,

I have a problem where I want to sample from a distribution that is loosely speaking a "two-sided Gaussian" -- it is composed of the left half of a gaussian of width sigma2 and the right half of a gaussian of width sigma 1. The right half is to be scaled so that its peak is the same as that of the left. So the distribution looks like a Gaussian that is asymmetric about its peak.

I think a way to do this is to use a mixture of two truncated Gaussians with mixture fractions equal to sigma1/(sigma1+sigma2) and sigma2/(sigma1+sigma2)

The distribution for the left side is y ~ normal(mu,sigma1) T[,mu], so that it has support only on the left side of the peak
The distribution for the right side is y ~ normal(mu,sigma2) T[mu,], so that it has support only on the right side of the peak

I implemented the mixture by drawing a uniform random variable called mixingParam; if it's less than sigma1/(sigma1+sigma2), I draw from the first distribution and otherwise I draw from the second.

The complication is that y and mu and sigma are really vectors.

After reading the sections in the Stan manual about truncated distributions and mixtures, I implemented this in my Stan model.

The model compiles, but it doesn't sample, returning the error below.
